name: Congenitally Uncorrected Transposition of the Great Arteries with Cardiac Malformation
aliases: Congenital Transposition of the Great Arteries with Associated Cardiac Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Transposition of the Great Arteries

criteria.description: Discordant ventriculoarterial connection with the aorta arising from the morphological right ventricle and the pulmonary artery from the morphological left ventricle
Discordant atrioventricular connection with the morphological right atrium connected to the morphological left ventricle and vice versa
Presence of additional cardiac malformations such as ventricular septal defect, pulmonary stenosis, or tricuspid valve abnormalities
Echocardiographic evidence confirming anatomical discordance and associated defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ventriculoarterial and atrioventricular discordance with at least one associated cardiac malformation confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities including echocardiography and cardiac MRI.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cyanosis due to systemic venous blood entering systemic circulation
pathognomonic.notes: Central cyanosis is a hallmark in uncorrected TGA
searchTerms: cyanosis due to venous blood bypass

pathognomonic.symptomName: Single loud second heart sound (S2) due to aortic valve closure

searchTerms: abnormal heart sound from septal defect
failure to gain weight as baby

common.symptomName: Heart murmur due to tricuspid valve abnormalities
searchTerms: heart murmur from tricuspid valve problem
symptoms of high lung blood pressure

rare.symptomName: Stroke or embolic events secondary to intracardiac shunting
searchTerms: embolic events caused by intracardiac shunt

rare.symptomName: Hepatomegaly due to right heart failure
searchTerms: enlarged liver from right heart failure

rare.symptomName: Exercise intolerance progressing to heart failure
searchTerms: difficulty exercising progressing to heart failure
poor stamina leading to heart problems

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance
Cardiac MRI confirming anatomical details and associated malformations
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings
other: Electrocardiogram showing abnormal conduction or arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Physiological correction with atrioventricular and ventriculoarterial discordance but preserved circulation
Pulmonary stenosis with ventricular septal defect and overriding aorta
Different anatomical configuration and clinical presentation

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy
Sudden onset arrhythmias or complete heart block
references: Anderson RH, et al. The anatomy of congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. Cardiol Young. 2006.
Warnes CA. Transposition of the great arteries. Circulation. 2006.
